Officer Webb was using the ATM at the Bank of America on the corner of [NAME] and [NAME], and I was pulling out of the parking lot in front of him. Officer Webb turned his lights on and motioned for me to pull over immediately after leaving the parking lot. I followed the instructions provided. Office Webb then pulled his cruiser in front of my vehicle and approximately 20 other vehicles, blocking both lanes of traffic (two way street). Officer Webb walked up to my vehicle and started yelling at me for taking a left turn out of the parking lot. Although I didn't argue with him, and proceeded to shout at me for "not paying attention." I apologized instinctively, attempting to calm this officer down. He then proceeded to mock me by saying "oh really, you didn't know. you didn't see it. that sign has been there for ten years." I apologized again, and let the P.O. know I wasn't arguing with him. Despite all this, Officer Webb continued to yell at me in front of what I would estimate to be 20 or so vehicles who were in line behind me. At this point Office Webb still hadn't asked for my drivers license or registration. he was just standing in the middle of the road continuing to yell at me in the same mocking tone. I informed Office Webb that he was acting inappropriately. I told him he was clearly not in control of his emotions/rage and that his behaviors was out‐of‐line. I asked for his badge number, and he responded by repeating his badge number over and over again in a rushed fashion, clearly knowing I couldn't possibly remember. When I finally got a pen, he simply responded by telling me "I'll do one better" in the same agitated and escalated demeanor. He then gave me a business card. I pointed out he was blocking two lanes of traffic and about 20 cars yelling at someone for not seeing a left turn sign, and asked him to write the ticket if he intended to do so. He finally asked for my license and registration, retreated to his car after the line of traffic started honking horns, and pulled forward and took a right onto [NAME] St where he proceeded to write my ticket. It was at this point I called the non‐emergency line to the police department and requested a leadership figure to come out and calm down this P.O.. I then proceeded to take video and still photos of the incident, including the line of cars, the remarks drivers were yelling from their card/honking to show the supervisor upon arrival. The P.O. returned before the supervisor arrived and gave me the ticket. Without saying a word he turned around and left. I did drive to the local police department to report the incident and show my video and still photos. However, given how strongly the police office acted, I felt it was necessary to write a formal complaint. I have complete respect for P.O.s and the work they do. West Roxbury is a firmly older irish‐catholic neighborhood with many retired P.O.s and firefighters. Officer Webb's behavior does not reflect well on the police department. It is for this reason I took the time to write a formal complaint regarding my interaction with Office Webb. Not only was he clearly not in control of his emoons, but he did it in front of 20 other vehicles and pedestrians in a blue color neighborhood where so many other P.O.s and firefighters have rered aer years of service.

As a result of a preliminary detail investigation that was conducted on Wednesday, January 5, 2022, into a questioned invoice by Accutemp Engineering with regard to Officer Eliana Builes, I performed another preliminary investigation with regard to an assigned detail for RJV Construction Corporation performed on August 23, 2021 at 4 Falcon Street on District A-7. ¶ A request for two officers was made by Mr. Victor Pacella, Project Manager, for RJV Construction.  The detail was assigned to Officers Eliana Builes and John Pels on the day of the detail, August 23, 2021.  The details were assigned at 08:25 hours and 09:45 hours respectively. ¶ Officer Builes submitted a detail card, tracking number 2441604, with a start time of 08:30 hours and an end time of 09:00 hours and marked the detail card “No Show” for a total of 30 minutes worked. ¶ Officer Pels submitted a detail card, tracking number 2441605, with a start time of 10:15 hours and an end time of 15:00 hours for a total of 4 hours and 45 minutes worked. ¶ Note: ¶ 1.	Officer Builes’ detail card was verified on October 6, 2021, 44 days after the detail was performed. ¶ 2.	Officer Pels’ detail card was verified on September 2, 2021, 10 days after the detail was performed. ¶ After reviewing the detail card submissions, I contacted Mr. Victor Pacella at RJV Construction about the assigned details.  Mr. Pacella stated that their records indicate that only one officer worked the assigned detail at 4 Falcon Street on August 23, 2021.  Mr. Pacella also stated the construction crew worked the entire day from 07:30 hours to 15:00 hours. ¶ Based on our conversation, I requested that Mr. Pacella document our conversation in writing on a department letter head, scan, and email to me.  Mr. Pacella was concerned about the response the RJV Construction would receive from police officers if he documented the reported issue.  I informed Mr. Pacella that the Boston Police Department would investigate any reported misconduct.  Mr. Pacella stated he would provide the requested letter with supporting documents. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 23 of Rule 102 (Truthfulness). Officer Builes was Untruthful by submitting a detail card with the actual start time of 08:30 and an actual end time of 09:00 hours as true and accurate. Officer Builes was also untruthful by marking “No Show” on the detail card. ¶ •	Officer Builes’ detail card submission is in direct conflict to the hours worked by RJV Construction.  RJV started work at 07:30 hours and worked until 15:00 hours. Coupled with the fact ¶ that Officer John Pels did work the assigned detail. Officer Builes’ submission of a “No Show” detail card reflecting she performed the detail from 08:30-09:00 hours cannot be accurate ¶ giving RJV was on-site at 07:30 hours and Officer Pels arrived at 10:15 hours. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 3 of Rule 102 (Conduct). Officer Builes’ Conduct was unbecoming as it did not reflect favorably on the Department. ¶ •	Officer Builes knowingly submitted the detail card with tracking number 2441604 with a start time of 08:30 hours and an end time of 09:00 hours. Mr. Pacella provided a letter stating ¶ their records only indicate that Officer Pels worked the assigned detail. Officer Builes’ conduct can be construed as acceptable behavior by contractor and the general public.  It gives the ¶ false appearance that a Boston Police Officer can submit a detail card and expect compensation for a detail that was not worked. ¶ Officer Builes violated Special Order 15-014 later re-issued under Special Order 18-031. ¶ •	Officer Builes did not submit the detail card for verification until 44 days after the scheduled detail date.  Officer Builes was required to submit her detail card within 96 hours (4 days). ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 7 of Rule 325 (Detail Cards). ¶ •	Officer Builes did not submit the detail card with tracking number 2467807 that accurately reflected the actual hours worked.  RJV does not have any record of Officer Builes working the ¶ assigned detail at 4 Falcon Street on August 23, 2021. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 5 (Cannon 7 of Ethics) of Rule 113. ¶ •	Officer Builes submission of the detail card with tracking number 2467807 for indication that she had performed the detail, but not having performed the assigned detail at 88 Kingston ¶ Street on August 23, 2021 is a corrupt act. ¶ Officer Pels violated Special Order 15-014 later re-issued under Special Order 18-031. ¶ •	Officer Pels did not submit the detail card for verification until 10 days after the scheduled detail date.  Officer Pels was required to submit her detail card within 96 hours (4 days).
